conviction_note: The Q1 headline is already public: revenue was pre-announced on 2026-10-20 at $18.5-19.5bn against a $14.5-15.5bn guide. So the print turns on the FY27 guide, which stays at $65-72bn with consensus at about $70.3bn even though Q1 alone runs at a $76bn annual rate, and on whether the Q2 gross margin guide falls back. The arithmetic of a raise and the AI read from a counterparty (Celestica) lean up. Margin mean-reversion, a new CFO giving his first guide and a 16.7-point put skew lean down. The findings sum to +0.5, the scaled number is +0.6 (p_up 52 times abs 15), the two agree, and both are small against a 13.7% implied move.
bar: Q1 FY27: the company's own preliminary range, revenue $18.5-19.5bn and GM 12.0-12.5% (https://ir.supermicro.com/news/news-details/2026/Supermicro-Provides-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2027-Preliminary-Business-Update/default.aspx, 2026-10-20). Pre-prelim consensus was $14.93bn revenue and $1.02 EPS (Benzinga snippet), which is stale. FY27: company guide $65-72bn (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/12/super-micro-guided-fiscal-2027-revenue-16-billion/), consensus $70.27bn from 15 analysts (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/smci/forecast/, read 2026-11-03). Q2 FY27 revenue consensus $16.20bn and EPS ~$1.01 come from one source (Benzinga, via search snippet) and very likely predate the 10-20 pre-announcement, so the Q2 bar is effectively unsourced. Guidance findings are capped for that reason.
positioning_check: Short interest: 91.2M shares, 1.4 days to cover at the 2026-08-14 settlement (Curved Trading/FINRA snippet; the page itself returned 403). Equibles shows 16.15% of float and 3.0 days, period undated. No October settlement was reachable: Nasdaq returned 503. On that basis this is a large but not crowded short on a very liquid name (35.6M shares a day). Skew: +16.69 vol points of 25-delta put over call, so the market is paying up for downside. Put/call open-interest ratio 0.23 means open interest is heavily calls. Tape: -26.9% over 20 sessions and -9.45% over 5, spot $31.77, below the $32.47 close the day before the +9.55% pre-announcement pop. The whole pre-announcement gain has been given back. SOXX fell 9.6% over the month (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/big-tech-capex-scorecard-amazon-spends-over-77-b-in-one-quarter-how-it-stacks-up-with-msft-tsla-googl/cZUh1oAR9Rr, 2026-10-30), so part of the drawdown is sector beta.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 was pre-announced at $18.5-19.5bn revenue (midpoint $19.0bn, +27% over the $15.0bn guide midpoint and over the ~$14.93bn consensus) and 12.0-12.5% gross margin against a 10.4-10.8% guide. The final print is expected to land inside that range, so the reported-quarter headline is public.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The pre-announcement itself moved the stock +9.55% on 2026-10-21 (baseline history row 2026-10-20). The gain was fully given back by 2026-11-03: spot $31.77 against the $32.47 close of 10-20. Q4 FY26 also missed on revenue but beat on EPS and margin, and the stock rose +19% on the FY27 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. It was on the wire and drew a 9.55% reaction. Only a final number outside the range (top end or above $19.5bn, or GM above 12.5%) would be new. The company gave no EPS in the pre-announcement, so EPS is the one Q1 line left open.
findings.independence: Same document as the guidance finding's Q1 arithmetic. The 10-21 to 10-22 tape reaction is reported by https://www.kucoin.com/blog/smci-stock-forecast-2026-analyst-price-targets-ai-demand-and-key-risks (2026-10-23).

findings.finding: The FY27 guide is still $65-72bn and was not updated in the pre-announcement. With Q1 at ~$19bn, holding that range implies the remaining three quarters average $15.3-17.7bn, below Q1's run rate. Consensus already sits at $70.27bn, near the top. Either the company raises the guide above $72bn (Q1 annualises to ~$76bn, on a backlog of over $60bn of new orders booked in Q4 FY26) or holding it signals Q1 was pulled forward. The stock giving back the whole pre-announcement pop says the market is leaning toward pull-forward.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has driven this name's big moves. In Aug 2026 a first FY27 guide of $65-72bn against ~$52.5bn consensus gave +19.02% (baseline 2026-08-11). In Nov 2025 an FY26 guide raise came with a Q1 double miss and the stock fell -11.33%. The 2026-02-03, 2026-05-05 and 2026-07-21 prints all gave +13.8% to +24.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected a raise to roughly $75bn+, the stock would sit above the post-pre-announcement high of $35.57, not 11% below it and below the pre-announcement close. The 16.7-point put skew says the market is paying up for a guide that is held or a Q2 that is light. A raise therefore sits partly against the skew. The Q2 consensus ($16.2bn) looks stale from before the pre-announcement, so the bar for Q2 is not well defined either way.
findings.independence: The FY27 consensus of $70.27bn is from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/smci/forecast/ (read 2026-11-03). Corroborating demand: Celestica raised its 2026 outlook and set a $40bn 2027 outlook on 2026-10-26 (separate finding). Against it: the pre-announcement's own risk language flags a concentrated customer base and lower-margin large deals.

findings.finding: Gross margin is at risk of mean-reverting in the Q2 guide. Q4 FY26 printed 17.5%, which commentators attribute to one-offs and delayed deals. Q1 FY27 was pre-announced at 12.0-12.5%, from customer and product mix. FY26 as a whole was only 10.8%. Memory cost inflation is also hitting server OEMs: Barclays cut Dell and HPE on 2026-10-14/15, saying OEM revenue growth is inflated by component prices, and SMCI fell 5-7% in sympathy. A Q2 GM guide back near ~10%, or memory-driven pressure, is the main downside line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin disappointments drove the sell-offs of Nov 2025 (-11.33%, GM 9.3-9.5%) and Aug 2025 (-18.29%). Goldman's Jan 2026 Sell call on margin erosion cost ~5-7% on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced already: the skew and the 27% drawdown carry some of it. What is not public is the Q2 margin guide itself. If the market had fully priced a reversion to ~10%, the pre-announced 12-12.5% would have been treated as a gift and held its pop, rather than being given back.
findings.independence: The Q4 FY26 17.5% being one-off: https://www.tikr.com/de/blog/super-micro-is-down-32-in-a-year-is-it-time-to-sell-or-load-up (updated 2026-10-28). The GM history is in the company's own pre-announcement and in the Q4 report. This is an industry-memory proxy for SMCI specifically; the company has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: The CFO was replaced with immediate effect on 2026-10-14 (8-K Item 5.02): Mark Long, ex-Western Digital CFO, succeeds David Weigand, and no reason was given. The 11-03 call is the new CFO's first guide, three weeks into the job. That raises the chance of a conservative, held FY range rather than a raise. Replacing Weigand had been planned since the 2024 accounting review.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print had a CFO this new. When the plan to replace the CFO was announced in late 2024 alongside the accounting review, the stock rose (stock3 commentary, about +20% that day), so a CFO change alone has not been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K is public, and the stock fell ~5-7% on 10-14/15, though wire copy put that move down to the Barclays OEM downgrades rather than to the CFO. What the 8-K does not show is how a three-week-old CFO will set the guide. That is inference, not a document.
findings.independence: Shares the theme of the guidance finding but not its document. The 2024 plan to replace the CFO: https://news.streetbeat.com/article/41738218.

findings.finding: Celestica, an AI-infrastructure peer reporting after SMCI's pre-announcement, beat on Q3 2026 (revenue $5.83bn against $5.46bn expected, EPS $3.30 against $2.97). Its Compute and Storage revenue rose 242%. It raised 2026 to $21.0bn and set a $40bn 2027 outlook (+90%), saying customer forecasts for 2028 are meaningfully higher. That supports the case that AI-rack demand runs past one quarter and is not a pull-forward.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline data on SMCI's reaction to peer prints. Peer and sector moves have repeatedly dragged SMCI 4-8% on the day (Dell/HPE downgrades 10-14/15, AI hardware sell-offs 09-14 and 09-28).
findings.why_not_priced: SMCI fell ~9% over the five sessions after this print, so the market did not carry Celestica's demand read across. Celestica serves different hyperscalers (largely ASIC/networking), which makes this a proxy.
findings.independence: Proxy, not an SMCI counterparty confirmation. Also reported in https://thelogic.co/briefing/celestica-expects-sales-to-nearly-double-next-year-as-ai-demand-surges/.

findings.finding: Hyperscaler capex in the Q3 reports of 2026-10-28/29 was mixed. Amazon spent $77.3bn (about $20bn above estimates) and said 2027 capex will be 'meaningfully more'. Alphabet held 2026 at $200bn. Microsoft cut its fiscal-year capex to $170bn from $175bn. SOXX fell 9.6% over the month.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AI sentiment sell-offs have hit SMCI repeatedly in 2026 (09-14, 09-28, 07-17). No direct history of its reaction to hyperscaler capex prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and largely priced: the -9.45% over five days happened through these prints. Net of the Microsoft cut it nearly offsets, so it is filed near zero.
findings.independence: Proxy, macro-to-company. SMCI's largest customers are not confirmed to be these four companies.

findings.finding: The setup into the print is deflated. Spot is $31.77, -26.9% over 20 days and below the pre-announcement close ($32.47), even though the pre-announced quarter is 27% above guide. The stock trades at ~7.5x forward P/E against a 14.7 five-year average (TIKR), and open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.23). On the other side, the 25-delta skew is +16.7, so the option market leans down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Five of the last five reactions were positive (+9.6 to +24.5%), each from a drawn-down level. The three before them were negative. Beats have been bought on this name in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew says the downside is not fully priced. The reason to doubt it: a 27% drawdown in 20 sessions, much of it sector beta (SOXX -9.6% over the month), has already delivered most of what a held guide would cost. The pre-announcement pop being fully round-tripped is visible evidence that holders already discount a pull-forward. Because the sign runs against the skew, it is sized small.
findings.independence: The tape numbers are from the sealed baseline. Sector beta: the stocktwits capex scorecard (2026-10-30). Short interest could not be verified as of October.

findings.finding: Working-capital and financing trail. On 2026-06-30 inventory was $12.9bn (from $4.68bn) and receivables $6.13bn (from $2.20bn). FY26 operating cash flow was -$6.81bn, non-cancellable purchase commitments ~$34.2bn, and cash $7.5bn against $8.7bn of debt and converts. The June raise was $5.6-7bn in equity and convertible preferred, with common placed at $27.50. The Q1 balance sheet in the release will show further build.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The June 2026 $7bn equity plan cost nearly 10% on the day. The ramp it funded then printed $11.1bn in Q4 and ~$19bn in Q1.
findings.why_not_priced: Known from the 10-K. Asked what the money buys: a ramp, corroborated by Q1 revenue at 27% above guide and a backlog of over $60bn in new orders. So the sign is zero, not negative. Only a new raise announced with the print would make this negative, and nothing on EDGAR points to one (no S-3 or 424B seen in the recent filing list).
findings.independence: The balance-sheet figures also appear in https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/12/super-micro-guided-fiscal-2027-revenue-16-billion/ (inventory $12.9bn, receivables $6.1bn, cash $7.5bn against debt $8.7bn).

findings.finding: Customer concentration. One customer was 28.1% of FY26 revenue and one supplier 63.1% of purchases (10-K). The pre-announcement itself flags a more concentrated customer base and lower margins on larger deals, and Q1's upside came from AI platform demand. That makes Q2 lumpiness a risk for the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In the Dec-2025 quarter one data-center customer was ~63% of revenue and GM fell to 6.3%. Lumpy large deals caused the 2025 delivery-delay misses (Aug 2025 -18.29%).
findings.why_not_priced: Known risk-factor material, largely priced. The new information would be Q1's 10%-customer share, disclosed with the print or in the 10-Q.
findings.independence: Shares a document with the financing finding. The concentration language also appears in the pre-announcement's forward-looking statements (ir.supermicro.com, 2026-10-20).

findings.finding: Export-control overhang. The March 2026 indictment of a co-founder and two associates (the company was not named a defendant) cost 33% on 03-20. The board's internal review finished 2026-08-20, but the 10-K says other government investigations are still open, and a material weakness in IT controls is still being tested in FY27. A disclosure update can come with the 10-Q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-03-20 indictment: -33% in one day. Governance and auditor events have caused this name's largest single-day falls.
findings.why_not_priced: Tail risk only. No new document points to a development in the window, so it is filed small with a fat left tail.

outside_window.finding: Taiwan ODM October monthly revenues (Wiwynn, Quanta, Foxconn) publish around 2026-11-05 to 11-10, after the exit window. They would read through on AI-rack demand.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly up, through the arithmetic of an FY27 raise and a fully round-tripped pre-announcement pop. That cuts against the +16.7 put skew and agrees with a contrarian reading of the -27% 20-day run-up. The skew keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar): the Q2 consensus is single-source and stale from before the pre-announcement. FY guidance finding capped from +2.0 to +1.5.
Lessons 1/6 (inside what the company already told the market): Q1 reported-quarter finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1.

Lesson 7 (skew and short interest): the positioning finding runs against a 16.7-point put skew, cut from +0.8 to +0.5 with the reason stated. Short interest is meaningful (~16% of float per Equibles, undated), so the negatives were shrunk: gross margin -1.5 to -1.2, CFO -0.8 to -0.6.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the working-capital build funds a ramp corroborated by Q1 at 27% above guide, so -0.3 became 0.0.

Lesson 5 (proxies smaller): Celestica cut from +0.8 to +0.6. The hyperscaler-capex finding went from +0.4 to +0.1, mostly because of new evidence found after the draft (the Microsoft capex cut in the 2026-10-30 scorecard), not the lesson alone.
p_up moved from 53 to 52 (toward 50 for the skew); abs_move_pct stayed at 15.
